name: import-linter-2c00e871-blind30
instr:
# import-linter-regen

We use this tool to write down which parts of a codebase are allowed to depend on which, and to fail a run when one of those rules is broken. Since a batch of unrecorded changes landed it gets almost everything wrong. Nothing about our projects changed and nothing about the settings we hand it changed. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. A run over a project that has always passed now comes back with a failure status.

Start with the file in which we write the rules down. Every value taken from one written as headed blocks of name-and-value lines keeps the blank space that surrounded it, so a name typed with a space after the equals sign matches nothing. Asking instead for that file's contents to be handed back to a caller returns something other than what it states about the blocks of rules it holds, with the part taken from a block's own heading coming out wrong. Where we give a setting that accepts one of a fixed list of words a value outside that list, the message naming what was expected is no longer produced: the run falls over with a type error while that message is being worded, and values differing only in case, which used to be turned away with that message, hit the same crash. Where we arrange packages into ordered levels, marking one of them as allowed to be absent by wrapping its name in brackets loses the first letter of the name, so the wrapped one is treated as a different, non-existent name and a safeguard for co
